The *Aññatarātissātherīgāthā* (Thig 1.5) is a short verse text preserved in the *Therīgāthā* ("Verses of Senior Nuns") within the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated widely in modern scholarship, with thirteen translations across ten languages cataloged on SuttaCentral, including English translations by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

However, curated records on SuttaCentral identify an extensive series of resembling parallels across multiple Buddhist textual traditions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon itself, resembling passages occur in the *Akkhaṇasutta* (AN 8.29), the *Uṭṭhāna Sutta* (Snp 2.10 / PTS Snp 57), and the *Theragāthā* collections of Khadiravaniya Revata (Thag 14.1) and Sāriputta (Thag 17.2) [SuttaCentral]. Resembling verses also appear widely in Dharmapada and Udānavarga lineages, including the Pali Dhammapada (Dhp 315), the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (G-Dhp 97–134, *Maguvagga*), the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 216–238, *Śaraṇavagga*), the Sanskrit and Tibetan Udānavarga recensions (UV 5, UVS 5, and Uv Kg 5, *Priyavarga*), and Chinese Buddhist canon translations, specifically T 210.30, T 212.6, and T 213.5 [SuttaCentral].
